audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may retain a noncash Aerospace tax benefit already monetized in the cash bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $53.9 million, equal to 87.8% of the $61.4 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inflates anchor OE while the bridge separately adds $1,242.48 million of cash and short-term investments reflecting after-tax Aerospace proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, the Company recognized a deferred tax asset of $ 53.9 million for the excess of the tax basis over the book basis of the Aerospace investment, in accordance with ASC 740‑30‑25‑9 and 25‑10.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the $53.9 million noncash deferred-tax benefit, but the supplied record does not demonstrate that it remains in OE. If retained, it would be a material double count because the sale proceeds added through the bridge were already reduced for estimated taxes.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE from continuing-operations income through cash adjustments, explicitly remove the $53.9 million benefit and rerun all scenarios if any portion remains in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: The asbestos insurance recognition may be an impermissible one-off inside the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.77 million net benefit, equal to 45.2% of the $61.4 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inflates anchor OE through the $35.8 million noncash insurance-recovery recognition net of the $8.03 million liability remeasurement.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the updated actuarial study, the Company estimated the loss recovery of indemnity and defense costs under the CIP agreement, and as such, the Company recognized an insurance recovery asset of $ 35.8 million, which was commensurate with the assumptions used to calculate the asbestos liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The one-time net benefit is demonstrated, but its treatment in the supplied OE calculation is not. Retaining it as recurring earnings would materially overstate value. Any normalization must still include sustainable net asbestos cash costs and recoveries; the June 2026 balance sheet shows a $34.59 million liability and $33.81 million recovery asset.
audit_findings.action: Trace both asbestos entries and actual settlement, defense and insurance cash flows through FY2025 OE; exclude the recognition gain, establish a normalized net cash allowance and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The historical OE series may mix pre-sale Aerospace earnings with post-sale continuing operations
audit_findings.mechanism: Could distort the historical OE series used to judge business stability, select growth assumptions and apply the too-hard conclusion, although the numerical anchor is FY2025 latest actual.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, the historical results for Aerospace are reported in the accompanying consolidated statement of income as a discontinued operation and the assets and liabilities have been retrospectively reclassified to assets and liabilities held for sale in the accompanying consolidated balance sheet.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates retrospective discontinued-operations presentation only for the periods presented, while the OE series extends to 2016. The record does not establish whether 2016–2022 were reconstructed on the current perimeter. Because the latest-actual anchor does not mechanically depend on the older values, the value effect cannot be established without the underlying calculations.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2016–2022 OE from continuing operations excluding Aerospace and compare the resulting history with the supplied series; then reassess the too-hard flag and growth scenarios without changing the FY2025 perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Cross-currency swap liabilities may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.0 million at June 30, 2026; $0.40 per diluted share and 0.71% of $2,105 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An outstanding derivative liability would reduce the equity bridge if it is not already netted, while associated net interest receipts enter equity-level OE through interest expense.
audit_findings.evidence: If a derivative is designated as a net investment hedge, such as the Company's cross-currency swaps, then the changes in the fair value of the derivative is recognized in other comprehensive income (loss) and will be subsequently reclassified to earnings when the hedged net investment is either sold or substantially liquidated.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates that the swaps remained outstanding after the Aerospace sale. Deducting the full $15.0 million would reduce base value from $55.77 to approximately $55.37 per share and the 30%-MOS threshold from $39.04 to approximately $38.76. The current $39.48 price remains above the buy-below threshold and far below estimated intrinsic value, so the valuation conclusion does not change.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the $15.0 million liability was not already included elsewhere in the bridge and record the deduction in the next bridge rerun if still outstanding.

audit_findings.title: Bankrupt legacy indemnitor could leave unmodeled Cequent liabilities
audit_findings.mechanism: Any liabilities no longer recoverable from the indemnitor would become claims ahead of common equity through the bridge or reduce future OE through settlement, remediation and defense cash costs.
audit_findings.evidence: If First Brands is unable to satisfy its indemnification obligations to us, we may incur unexpected liabilities relating to our legacy Cequent businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: The indemnitor's bankruptcy and resulting risk are demonstrated, but the supplied filings identify no specific reverted claim, reserve deficiency or probable loss. This is presently a forward-looking contingent exposure rather than a quantified valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Monitor the bankruptcy docket, proofs of claim, indemnification receivables, Cequent environmental and litigation matters, and subsequent-event disclosures; rerun only when a probable or reasonably estimable net exposure is established.

audit_findings.title: Repeated restructuring and systems spending must not be normalized away wholesale
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.2 million of disclosed FY2025 realignment/severance/consulting, systems and transaction costs, equal to 24.8% of the $61.4 million anchor; an additional $8.9 million was disclosed in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Excluding recurring portfolio-realignment, systems and transaction costs without a normalized allowance inflates anchor OE and projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We have executed meaningful realignment actions over the past few years to address variable and structural costs where demand has fallen.
audit_findings.explanation: Repeated spending is demonstrated across multiple years, including $15.2 million in FY2025 and $8.9 million in the first half of 2026. The record does not show which items were removed from OE, but wholesale exclusion could materially overstate sustainable earning power. Claimed future savings do not by themselves establish that these operating costs will disappear.
audit_findings.action: Audit every OE adjustment for these categories, separate genuinely completed one-time actions from recurring portfolio-management costs, derive a multi-year normalized cash allowance and rerun all scenarios.
